Investment memo · ALFEN-NL · for Richard

Alfen: a Dutch grid franchise to watch, not yet to buy, until the FY26 results on 17 February 2027 reset the entry price

3 November 2026. Price €10.38 (29 October 2026); 21.75m shares; market capitalisation about €226m. Enterprise value is about €220m on June 2026 lease-inclusive net cash of €6.2m, or about €245m (9.8x FY27 EBITDA) on a year-end net debt of about €20m. The Q3 2026 trading update is due on 4 November 2026 at 07:00 CET; nothing in this memo reflects it, and topic 8 sets out what to read in it. Definitions and sources are in the end notes.

0Summary: key insights, implications and conclusions

The case in brief. Alfen owns one business worth owning: a 70% share of Dutch secondary substations, whose volume will rise for years on a grid build-out that is dated in law and backed by the grid operators' budgets. Alfen also owns two businesses it would be better off without: a commoditising charger business and a storage integrator that the battery-cell makers are cutting out of the value chain. Those two businesses still make about 60% of gross profit and set the group's margin.

A credible chief executive from outside the company has done the cheap half of a turnaround (cost, cash, structure, quality) and has yet to show the expensive half (margin). Three things set the timing of the investment case. The earnings trough, in H2 2026, has not yet been reported. Consensus FY27 EPS is wrong because the brokers under-model one accounting line, depreciation and amortisation (D&A). The model's P/E-based return is an artefact of near-zero earnings. The positive skew Richard looks for exists, but it arrives in late 2027 and it rests on one line: grid volume.

The seven things that matter.

  1. 1
    Grid volume is the whole thesis, and the grid operators' capacity to install, not end demand, rations it. Alfen's substation volumes rose 27% year on year in Q2 2026 (883 units) after a 14% fall in FY25. The three Dutch grid operators plan 13% more installations a year to 2028 and have record budgets (Enexis alone €13bn to 2030), but two of the three installed 20-30% below plan in 2025 for want of technicians and permits. The forecasts assume grid volume growth of 8-11% a year. In the model, grid gross profit rises by €23.9m between FY26 and FY30, more than the group's total EBITDA gain of €23.0m: storage and charging together add less gross profit than opex inflation takes away. Alfen's grid moat protects its market share, not its price: three monopsony buyers hold the grid segment's gross margin at 22-25%.
  1. 2
    The earnings trough is ahead, not behind. The forecasts put H2 2026 EBITDA at about €1.9m (a 1.0% margin) against €12.5m a year earlier. Storage milestone revenue falls from €98.8m in H1 2026 to about €45m, and a €5-8m leadership overlap coincides with 5% wage indexation. The H1 2027 margin is forecast at 4.7% against 6.3% a year earlier, because the saving from ending the leadership overlap arrives in the same half as an unrepeatable storage comparison. The recovery first shows in H2 2027, at a 5.7% margin against 1.0%. The market knows the shape of the trough but not its depth: four of the eight brokers still imply H2 2026 EBITDA of €5-10m.
  1. 3
    Consensus FY27 EPS of €0.35 is about 85% too high, and the company's own accounts document the correction. Underlying D&A is about €21m, not the €13.5-17m that two of the five brokers with FY27 EPS estimates use. The €21m reconciles to the accounts: reported D&A was €22.2m in FY25 and €10.2m in H1 2026, and it is rising as about €10m a year of capitalised development starts to amortise. With D&A at €21m, the consensus median FY27 EPS falls to about €0.20 before any EBITDA cut, and to about €0.08-0.12 after the FY26 EBITDA base is reset (consensus FY26 EBITDA is €22.0m against the forecasts' €18.3m). The FY26 annual report on 17 February 2027 will force the correction. No broker has written about the D&A gap.
  1. 4
    Operating leverage is both the profit engine and the main hazard. Alfen earns a 26-27% contribution margin on about €100m of fixed opex, and carries €23-24m of fixed charges (D&A, leases, interest) below EBITDA. EBITDA must therefore exceed about €23m before Alfen earns any net profit. A 10% change in revenue moves EBITDA by 40-50% and EPS by several times that. The FY27 EBITDA range of outcomes is €16-34m around a base of €25m; the FY27 EPS range is -€0.26 to +€0.38 around a base of €0.06.
  1. 5
    The valuation must be read on EBITDA, and on that basis the shares are cheap for a reason but not cheap enough for this setup. The model's returns of +92% (to end-2027) and +172% (to mid-2029) apply the 45.37x guideline P/E for a "Reinforcing" lifecycle phase to two-year-forward EPS of €0.44 and €0.62. With EPS this close to zero, a P/E carries no information, and the stock is not in the Reinforcing phase. On EV/EBITDA the shares trade at about 9.8x FY27 EBITDA, 39% below their own history. At 9-10x FY28 EBITDA (€30.7m) the shares are worth €11.5-12.9 at end-2027 (+11% to +24%); at the 7x trough multiple they are worth €8.7, and at a 13x precedent-transaction multiple €17.1. Three years out, 9-10x FY30 EBITDA (€41.3m) gives €16-18 a share (+55% to +70%) if grid volume grows 8-11% a year, and about €11.5 (flat) if it grows 5% a year. My fair multiple is the ten-year median two-year-forward P/E of about 26x, which coincides with 9x FY28 EV/EBITDA, not the 90th-percentile 45x.
  1. 6
    The expectations gap works against the shares first and for them later. For six to nine months the unknowns are negative; beyond twelve months they are positive, and in sum the gap is favourable.
  1. 7
    The fit with Richard's six target setups is weak. The case is a hybrid of two setups. It is a "quality cyclical at trough-on-trough", which holds for the grid unit on a discounted EBITDA multiple, but the trough has not yet been reported. It is also a "corporate change-driven EPSU" case, which holds in management's actions but not yet in reported results. It fits none of the six target setups crisply.

Implication for Richard. Alfen is a dated watch-list case, not yet an entry case. Four concrete, near-term triggers would turn it into an entry case: a 2027 storage order book of €90m or more by December 2026; substation volumes above 950 a quarter; the FY26 D&A print and a consensus reset on 17 February 2027; and H2 2027 results that show grid volume carrying the margin. The asymmetry turns positive at roughly the 7x-EBITDA trough price of €8-9 a share, or after a reset that leaves consensus at or below the forecasts. The topics below give the evidence and the arithmetic; topic 6 sets out the five judgements that move the shares and what each is worth if wrong.

Scorecard: the Rater's grades for topics 1 to 12

1Operating environment: tailwinds and the absence of headwinds

Conclusion: grid has one real tailwind, dated in law but acting only on volume and rationed by the operators' labour; the two segments that make most of the gross profit face intensifying structural headwinds; and the sector factor is against the stock now. The net external effect is mildly negative for six to nine months and mildly positive after that.

Evidence.

  • Grid, for: Dutch distribution capex is rising from about €10bn a year to about €18bn in FY27 (ING), and more than 14,000 parties are queuing for grid connections. A fast-track regime for connections at 21kV and above has been in force since 7 October 2026, and permit-free substation expansion is legislated for "shortly after summer 2027". The EU ban on SF6 (sulphur hexafluoride) gas in new medium-voltage switchgear applies from January 2026, and Alfen's three substation lines are already certified SF6-free. A national plan targets 5,000 more grid technicians by 2030.
  • Grid, against: two of the three operators installed 20-30% fewer substations than planned in 2025, and Utrecht froze new connections in 2026. Management expects no FY26 volume effect from the fast-track regime. ING (2 November 2026) finds Dutch physical investment capped by space and by headroom for nitrogen emissions.
  • Storage, for: European utility-scale storage additions are projected to rise from 22 GWh (2024) to about 120 GWh (2029). RWE took the final investment decision on its 400MW Moerdijk project in September 2026, and German large-scale additions rose more than twentyfold year on year in September.
  • Storage, against: cell makers now sell turnkey systems; tenders draw up to 50 bidders; integrator margins are 10-20%; a renewed price war led by CATL (Bernstein, 23 October) makes buyers wait; lenders now want 30-60% engineering completion before financial close; and the Chinese export VAT rebate falls to zero on 1 January 2027.
  • Charging: European battery-electric vehicle registrations rose 59% in September 2026, yet Alfen's charge-point volumes fell 12% and its prices 6% in H1 2026, the seventh consecutive quarter of decline. Competitors grew: Zaptec by 26-32% and Easee by 33%. Value is migrating to site owners and software.
  • Macro and sector: grid shares fell 12-20% in October as momentum trades unwound, and the sector's relative-strength percentile fell from 69 to 14 in three weeks. Alfen's six-month R-squared to the grid basket has risen to 29%, with a beta of 1.24.

Inference. The one strong, dated tailwind acts on Alfen's segment with the lowest gross margin per euro of revenue, and it reaches Alfen at the operators' installation pace, not at the pace of their budgets. The two segments that set the group margin face intensifying structural headwinds. The sector factor is working against the stock now.

So what. External forces justify grid growth of 8-12% a year at flat margins, volatile storage volume with drifting margins, and flat-to-falling charging revenue. Nothing external supports a group gross margin above about 27%. The net external effect is negative for H2 2026 and H1 2027 and modestly positive from mid-2027, when the permit-free law starts to ease the permitting half of the operators' constraint. Labour is the other half of that constraint, and the labour supply moves slowly.

Counter-case. Alfen's turnkey transport distribution station attacks the operators' own bottleneck: it takes four months to install instead of more than a year, and Enexis is moving from about 10 to about 120 of these stations a year. Alfen can therefore grow faster than the operators' installer headcount. Private-customer demand frozen by grid congestion is a reservoir that permit-free expansion could release. Mobile storage sells into the congestion itself (Greener Power's fleet has passed 240 units, with vendor finance from DLL). If the operators install at their +13% plan from 2028, Alfen's grid revenue grows 13-15% a year, worth €3-4m a year of EBITDA above the base.

What would change my view. Operator 2027 plans (published December to February) with installation targets more than 10% above 2026 actuals; a dated parliamentary timetable for permit-free expansion; storage intake above €45m in a quarter; charging volumes flat year on year in Q4 2026.

Against the market. Consensus treats grid congestion as the story. I agree on the direction and disagree on how it reaches Alfen: the market reads the operators' budgets, while I read their technicians. On storage and charging, the sell-side knows the headwinds. What it under-weights is that the VAT-rebate removal and the price war hit in the same quarter (Q1 2027), and that the €80m guarantee facility (€52m used) caps how much large fixed-price storage work the balance sheet can take on.

Score: 46, set by the Rater. One strong, dated, law-backed tailwind (Dutch grid capex rising from about EUR 10bn to 18bn a year, permit-free substations from late 2027, the SF6 ban Alfen is already certified for) reaches only the grid unit, about 45% of revenue. It comes as volume only, rationed by the operators' technicians and permits (two of three installed 20-30% below plan in 2025), and three monopsony buyers hold its price. Against it, structural headwinds (cell makers selling turnkey, a renewed price war, VAT-rebate removal, charging prices in their seventh quarter of decline as value moves to site owners) act on the two units that make about 60% of gross profit. Consensus sales growth at the 80th percentile reflects the grid volume, but external forces give no support to group margin, so the net is slightly negative over two to three years: negative to mid-2027, mildly positive after. I am a touch above the External change forces group's 44 because the grid force is unusually well funded and dated.

2Internal corporate change forces and the absence of problems

Conclusion: the self-help is real, broad and well executed. It has done the cheap half of the turnaround (cost, cash, structure, quality) but not the expensive half (margin, guidance, growth), and the interim finance director is the open flank. The team is strong on inputs and unproven on outputs.

Evidence.

  • Leadership: Michael Colijn (previously at Heliox, which was sold to Siemens) has been chief executive since 1 October 2025 and has met every dated milestone: three accountable business units from 1 May 2026, with unit directors appointed in Q2; net cash; the CATL sodium-ion agreement (5 GWh, 16 July 2026); the Eve Plus charger platform listed at Rexel, Bouygues and Technische Unie; re-entry to the UK; and a launch in Southern Europe.
  • Cost and cash: headcount cut from 1,053 to 909; €13.1m of stated annual savings; other opex down 21% in FY25; net working capital from €159m (H1 2023) to €58m (12% of revenue); inventory from €151m to €62m; €79m of cash released; capex capped below 4% of revenue.
  • Portfolio and quality: DC chargers exited; AC charger platforms cut from five to three; mega-projects avoided; acquisitions paused; the moisture defect in the Pacto concrete housings resolved and Alfen's certified-supplier status restored.
  • Problems: the fourth finance director since January 2024 (Onno Krap left at short notice on 1 July 2026; Bart Meussen is interim); adjusted personnel cost up 6.1% in H1 2026 on a 14% smaller headcount, because of 5% wage indexation; a €5-8m leadership overlap in H2 2026; restructuring friction between the units; the management layer below the top cut from 58 to 54 people; incentives tied to revenue and adjusted EBITDA; no internal audit function; and no supervisory board shareholdings apart from the chair's 20,000 shares.

Inference. The change is genuine and broad, and it already shows in the balance sheet and in one operating metric (substation volumes). It has not reached the outputs that a corporate-change case must show: gross margin, EBITDA margin, EPS and guidance. The finance director's departure in the middle of the transformation keeps the risk of mis-execution live, and it means the team's forecasting credibility is unproven.

So what. Credit the team with cost control and working-capital discipline: the forecasts model opex tightly, capex at 3.3% of revenue and a flat share count. Give the team no credit yet for growth or for margin beyond the mechanical removal of the leadership overlap. The strategy is a repair plan, not a growth plan. Management's 2027 goal of "consistent profitable growth" means a year-on-year improvement in revenue and margin, a bar that revenue growth of 1% and a 4.1% margin would clear. BCG has examined the largest perimeter question, whether Alfen should own all three units, and answered yes.

Counter-case. Thirteen months of delivery on every dated promise is what a turnaround looks like before the numbers turn. The new unit structure already redeploys storage staff to grid work. The digital platform (remote service, ten-minute installations) lowers the cost of serving customers. A permanent finance director and numerical FY27 guidance in February 2027 would complete the reset. The forecasts' refusal to credit the commercial plan (UK, Southern Europe, turnkey, sodium-ion) is a deliberate choice; if the team is as good as its first year suggests, the risk to the forecasts is upward.

What would change my view. A permanent finance director with a listed-company record; numerical FY27 guidance with a margin of 6% or more; H1 2027 personnel cost at or below H2 2026; a stated plan for the two moatless units that goes beyond "focus".

Against the market. The sell-side gives the team the benefit of the doubt on normalisation in 2027. I give the team that benefit on cost and withhold it on growth, because the record shows that when Alfen beats expectations the cause is timing, and when it misses the cause is demand.

Score: 58, set by the Rater. Since October 2025 the outside chief executive has run a broad reset and met every dated milestone: three business units, headcount down from 1,053 to 909, EUR 13m of savings, working capital cut from EUR 159m to 58m, DC chargers exited and platforms rationalised, the CATL sodium-ion deal, and UK and Southern European launches. None of it has yet reached margin, EPS or guidance. The 2027 ambition has been cut to 'year-on-year improvement', this is the fourth finance director since January 2024, and the forecasts credit only about EUR 3m of net opex relief in FY27. I sit slightly above the group's 55 because the reset is far broader and better executed than a gentle drift, but the lagging outputs, the open finance seat and a repair rather than growth ambition keep it well short of a 75.

3Value chain, business model, financial profile, management

Conclusion: Alfen has a narrow, real moat in Dutch grid whose rent the buyers capture, beside two moatless hardware units; a below-average financial profile with a safe balance sheet; and a dynamic but unproven management with deliberately modest goals. These foundations are weak for a thesis that needs margin, and adequate for one that needs only volume.

Evidence.

  • Grid: Alfen supplies about 70% of Dutch secondary substations under four-to-eight-year framework agreements. It takes about 50% of Stedin's volume, and Enexis and Liander are each above 10% of group revenue (34.8% together). Its protection comes from physics (a concrete station weighs over 1,000 times as much as a charger), national grid codes, early involvement in the operators' specifications, SF6-free certification and relationships dating back to 1937. Against that, the frameworks carry no minimum volumes and index materials costs with a lag; Alfen cut the segment's gross-margin target from 25-40% to 20-30% "because large grid operators demand discount prices"; and the operators second-sourced during the 2024 Pacto production stop.
  • Charging: 200-300 suppliers compete. Alfen co-founded the Open Charge Point Protocol (OCPP), which removes customer lock-in by design. Entry-level wallbox prices have fallen from about €1,000 to under €500, and Alfen's charging gross margin of 39.5% is now below Zaptec's 41%.
  • Storage: CATL is Alfen's single source of cells under a 5 GWh framework to 2032, with a 5% penalty on unfulfilled volume. Pricing is back-to-back on cells, and tenders draw up to 50 bidders.
  • Financial profile: the EBITDA margin was 5.9% in FY25 against 18% in FY22 on the same revenue; the EBIT margin is about 1.5% and ROIC about 1-5%. Free cash flow came from working-capital release, which is now exhausted. Net cash excluding leases was about €44m at June 2026 and is expected to be €18m at December 2026. Cohort peers earn EBITDA margins of 15-33% and ROCE of 25-33%.
  • Management: the ambition has been deliberately cut from "€1bn of revenue and a 15-20% margin by 2027" to "year-on-year improvement". Revenue guidance was cut mid-year in three consecutive years (FY23 -12%, FY24 -22%, FY25 -8% against the initial midpoints). The last twelve months have been good on action. Pay is below the peer 25th percentile. Under the structuurregime (which has applied to Alfen since April 2024), the supervisory board, not the shareholders, appoints the management board, and the bylaws allow a 250-day response period.

Inference. Alfen has one moderately strong, slowly widening moat (grid), but the buyers capture its rent. The two other segments have no moat and no pricing power, yet still produce about 60% of gross profit. Both sit in the sector's losing archetype: "own the scarce thing, not the box", and "in charging, the site owner earns, the box maker does not". No self-reinforcing mechanism improves Alfen's results on its own; any improvement must come from management action. The financial profile is below average on every line except balance-sheet safety. Management is moving from a founder-era team with a poor record of capital allocation to an operator focused on repair, with a good first year.

So what. Value Alfen as a defensible, low-margin volume franchise plus two price-taking assemblers: on EBITDA, at a discount to grid peers for the 57% of revenue that comes from outside grid. The strategy is coherent and sensible but not bold. It has no answer to disintermediation by the cell makers beyond a new battery chemistry, and no plan for the charging software profit pool beyond the basics every supplier offers.

Counter-case. Management claims its integrated offer (substation plus storage plus charging for microgrids) is unique, and grid congestion creates demand for it. The turnkey capability genuinely widens the grid moat. First-mover status in sodium-ion batteries could differentiate Alfen in storage tenders from H2 2027. The Elkamo acquisition shows the team can buy well. A sum-of-the-parts buyer would pay 11-18x EBITDA for the grid unit alone.

What would change my view. Evidence of a turnkey premium in grid gross margin (sustained above 25%); a storage order won on technology rather than price; a decision to partner or separate the charging business.

Against the market. The sell-side and I agree on which businesses have moats. We differ on takeover risk: the market reads Alfen's lack of takeover defences as contestability, but the structuurregime and a change-of-control default in the credit facility make a hostile bid impractical. Any bid is therefore likely to be friendly and to run on the board's timetable.

Score: 28, set by the Rater. The value chain and moat come first. Alfen has one real but buyer-capped moat, about 70% of Dutch secondary substations, but it protects share and not price (the segment's gross-margin target was cut to 20-30%). Two moatless, price-taking hardware units in the sector's losing archetype still make about 60% of gross profit. Management is promising but unproven and has deliberately modest goals. The financial profile then confirms it: ROIC about 0% (9th percentile), EBITDA margin at the 6th percentile, operating margin down 14 points in three years (6th percentile), and new capital earning far below its cost. Only the net-cash balance sheet is sound. Low predictability counts against it too, so I sit inside the four groups (36/36/20/36).

4Conservatism of guidance, management of sell-side expectations, track record

Conclusion: guidance is set low but is not conservative against the evidence; management has left the sell-side above it; and the record is of cuts, not raises. The first event with two-way guidance risk is the FY26 results on 17 February 2027.

Evidence. FY26 guidance is revenue of €435-475m and an adjusted EBITDA margin of 4-7% (€17.4-33.3m). Management reiterated it in May, after a 13% beat on Q1 revenue, and again in August. It gives no numbers beyond FY26, and its 2027 "ambition" is qualitative.

Consensus FY26 EBITDA of €22.0m sits above the forecasts' €18.3m because ING, Stifel, KBC and Deutsche Bank (€21.7-26.1m) have not updated for management's steer on H2 2026. Management has flagged every near-term negative in advance: H2 softness, higher personnel cost, a closing window for storage orders, no fast-track volume in FY26 and no further inventory reduction. The record is poor: every guidance move since 2023 has been a cut or a withdrawal, there has been no raise under the new chief executive, the quarterly beats in 2026 came from storage timing, and the misses in 2025 came from demand and mix.

Inference. FY26 revenue guidance is conservative; the FY26 margin range is not, because the floor is likely and the midpoint is not. The FY27 bar of "year-on-year improvement" is conservative by construction and tells the market nothing. Management keeps the sell-side conservative only in part: it steers down candidly in words but has let half the brokers stay above the evidence in their numbers. There is no record of raising guidance.

So what. My probabilities are in the chart below. The most important one concerns FY27: if management gives numerical FY27 guidance on 17 February 2027, the range will probably bracket consensus (revenue of about €470-500m, a 5-7% margin) with the forecasts at its low end. That would recreate the FY23-FY25 pattern of a mid-year steer down.

Counter-case. "Set low and reiterate" is what a chastened management does for a year before it starts to beat. A wide 4-7% FY27 margin range would be met comfortably. A capital markets day in 2027 (about 35% probability) could set a credible high-single-digit margin ambition and rebuild the habit of raising guidance.

What would change my view. A FY27 range whose midpoint sits at or below the forecasts' 5.2% margin; a first raise, however small, on a beat that does not come from timing.

Against the market. The market expects nothing from guidance, which limits the damage if the Q3 update only reiterates it. The market has not priced a FY26 result at the 4% margin floor, or a FY27 range that is later cut.

Score: 24, set by the Rater. Since 2023 every guidance move has been a cut or a withdrawal: three consecutive mid-year revenue cuts (-12%, -22%, -8%) and no raise under the new chief executive. The 2026 beats were storage timing; the 2025 misses were demand. FY26 revenue guidance is conservative, but the margin midpoint (needing about EUR 8.6m of H2 EBITDA against an evidenced EUR 1.9m) is not. Management steers candidly in words but has let half the brokers stay above the evidence, which matches the Guidance group's 24 and sits a little below the Sell-side group's 32.

5Pricing power, operating leverage, financial leverage, cost-out and feedback loops

Conclusion: Alfen has no pricing power and no financial leverage, but very high operating leverage on a fixed cost base, with a layer of fixed charges below EBITDA. Profit therefore moves far more than revenue in both directions. The engine is real, and it is currently running in reverse.

Evidence. Of the six profit levers, only operating leverage is strong, and it is working against Alfen today.

Inference. Revenue growth does produce outsized profit growth, but entirely through the absorption of fixed costs, and the same mechanism has worked in reverse for three years. Each €10m of extra revenue adds about €2.6m of EBITDA in a single year. Over a multi-year path, opex inflation eats a third of that gain, so the realised drop-through from FY26 to FY30 is about 16-17% and the EBITDA margin rises only to 6.9%. Each €1m of EBITDA is worth €0.036 of EPS; in FY27, a 10% change in EBITDA moves pre-tax profit by about 150%.

So what. Grid is where the leverage is cleanest: the Almere plant can double its output, so each 10% of extra grid revenue (about €22m) adds about €5m of gross profit at almost no extra opex. Storage is where the leverage cuts hardest, because fixed project staff are set against lumpy milestone revenue. Alfen has no price lever, no balance-sheet lever and little cost lever left, so the forecast is a volume forecast with a cost overlay.

Counter-case. Jefferies' EBITDA margin of 9.6-10% by FY30 needs revenue growth of about 12% a year for four years, or a change of mix. That outcome is not impossible if permit-free expansion and the technician plan let the operators install at plan and the reservoir of frozen private projects is released. Temporary staff (about 15% of grid personnel) and the Dutch innovation box (an effective 9% tax rate on qualifying income) are small shock absorbers.

What would change my view. Grid gross margin above 25% on turnkey mix for two consecutive halves, which would signal a premium for a scarce service; opex held flat in FY28 on 8% revenue growth.

Against the market. The sell-side agrees on the operating leverage and models it. The differences lie below EBITDA, where the brokers' D&A estimates differ from each other by €7.5m, and in opex, where most brokers assume the whole €8m leadership overlap disappears and no cost comes back.

Score: 57, set by the Rater. This scores the structure. Operating leverage is real and proven both ways: a 26-27% contribution margin on about EUR 100m of largely personnel opex, plus EUR 23-24m of fixed charges below EBITDA, so 10% more or less revenue moves EBITDA 40-50% (the same EUR 440m of revenue gave 18% EBITDA in FY22 and 5.9% in FY25). The other gears are absent or negative: prices fall in charging, follow cells in storage and are capped in grid; there is no financial leverage; the big cost-out is already in the base; and the feedback loops run mostly negative. Opex inflation also eats about a third of the drop-through, so the forecast EPS-to-revenue ratio from a near-zero base overstates the gearing. That is above the level-50 mix on gearing alone, but well short of Judges Scientific's 72-type proven leverage with stable pricing.

6Forecast financials: scope for double-digit growth and for higher growth and margins than the past

Conclusion: the forecasts show a slow, grid-led recovery, with double-digit EPS growth from near zero but no double-digit revenue growth and no return to past margins. The forecasts are sound; they sit below consensus where consensus is stale or mis-modelled; and they carry upside only if the new team's commercial plan works.

By half year, the forecasts show H2 2026 revenue down 12% with EBITDA of €1.9m (a 1.0% margin), H1 2027 revenue down 10% at a 4.7% margin, and H2 2027 revenue up 23% at a 5.7% margin.

No double-digit revenue growth. Revenue compounds at about 6.5% a year from FY25 to FY30. The one segment growing near double digits (grid, +8-11% a year) is only 43-50% of the mix, and the other two segments grow between nil and mid-single digits.

EPS growth is mechanical. EPS rises tenfold, from €0.06 in FY27 to €0.60 in FY30, but only because €23-24m of fixed charges are spread over a larger EBITDA. EBITDA-to-net-income conversion rises from 5% in FY27 to 32% in FY30, against 67% in FY22.

Margins do not return to the past. The EBITDA margin reaches 6.9% by FY30, against 11-18% in FY21-FY23, because the change of mix behind two-thirds of the FY22-FY25 margin collapse (charging falling from 57% of revenue to about 22%) does not reverse. Against the last four years (FY22-FY25: revenue flat, margin from 18% to 6%), both growth and margin improve; against the company's longer history, both are modest.

Free cash flow is about nil. On a full definition (after about €10m of capitalised development, about €6m of leases, restructuring and working capital for growth), free cash flow is about nil in aggregate to FY30. The consensus FCF figures (€13.7m, €2.5m and €8.1m) use FactSet's narrower definition and are not cash available to shareholders.

Where the forecasts sit against consensus. The forecasts are close to consensus on revenue (1-3% below), 15-17% below on FY26 and FY27 EBITDA, 8% below on FY28 EBITDA, and 85% and 34% below on FY27 and FY28 EPS. Most of the FY27 EBITDA gap (€3.7m of €4.2m) is inherited from the lower FY26 base; the forecast increase in FY27 EBITDA (+€6.7m) matches the consensus increase (+€7.2m). The EPS gap comes from D&A first and from EBITDA second.

The five judgements that move the shares, with the arithmetic. The FY27 base is EBITDA of €25.0m and EPS of €0.06. Each €1m of EBITDA is worth €0.036 of EPS (at a 22% tax rate and 21.8m shares). At 9x EV/EBITDA, each €1m of FY28 EBITDA is worth about €0.41 a share.

  1. 1
    Grid volume: the forecasts take grid revenue growth of 10% in FY27 and 11% in FY28, which assumes the operators install faster than their 2025 pace and slower than their plan. At +5% growth, grid revenue falls by €10.6m, gross profit (at 23.5%) by €2.5m and EBITDA by about €2.7m, and EPS falls by €0.10 to -€0.04. At +15%, EBITDA rises by €2.7m and EPS by €0.10 to €0.16. A 20-30% call-off cut at one operator, as happened in 2025, would cut grid revenue by €20-40m, EBITDA by €5-10m and EPS by €0.18-0.36. Carried to FY30, grid growth of 5% a year instead of 8-11% takes FY30 EBITDA from €41.3m to about €30m (a 5.4% margin), and the FY30 value at 9x from about €16 to about €11.5 a share. Grid volume alone is the difference between a 55% three-year return and no return.
  1. 2
    Storage intake: the forecasts take about €35m of orders a quarter from Q3 2026 and FY27 storage revenue of €140m, of which €56m is already in the 2027 backlog. At €50m a quarter, storage revenue is about €160m, gross profit rises by €4.3m (at 21.5%), EBITDA reaches €29.3m and EPS €0.21; at 9x FY28 EBITDA the same swing is worth about €1.8 a share (17%). At €20m a quarter, storage revenue is about €115m (the backlog plus mobile storage set the floor), EBITDA €19.6m and EPS -€0.13. Unless the guarantee facility is enlarged, its €28m of headroom truncates the upper branch. Storage intake is the widest single swing in the next 18 months and the least predictable.
  1. 3
    Opex: the forecasts remove €5m of the leadership overlap (Jefferies estimates €8m) and assume 3.5% wage indexation. If the full €8m goes and indexation is 3%, opex is €98.6m, EBITDA rises by €2.6m and EPS reaches €0.15. If half the overlap is permanent (new unit directors, a chief operating officer and a chief human-resources officer), opex is about €103.7m, EBITDA falls by €2.5m and EPS is -€0.03. The test is H1 2027 personnel cost against H2 2026.
  1. 4
    Charging: the forecasts assume unit volume turns to +7% on a 4% lower price, giving revenue growth of 3% at a 39.0% gross margin. At the consensus revenue growth of 7%, EBITDA rises by €1.6m and EPS reaches €0.12. If prices take another leg down (average selling price -8%, volume -2%, gross margin 38%), charging revenue is about €93m, gross profit falls €6.1m below the base, EBITDA is €18.9m and EPS -€0.16. Each point of charging gross margin is worth about €1.1m of EBITDA.
  1. 5
    D&A: this is a judgement about consensus, not about Alfen; the forecasts take €21.0m, reconciled to the accounts. At the €17m that the EPS brokers use, EPS rises by €0.14 to €0.20. At €23m, if the €8.4m of development in progress starts to amortise faster, EPS falls by €0.07 to -€0.01. For the consensus median, D&A at €21m alone takes FY27 EPS from €0.35 to about €0.20, and the FY26 base reset then takes it to €0.08-0.12.

Combined. If the three operating downsides (judgements 1, 2 and 4 at their low ends) all occur, FY27 EBITDA is about €11m and EPS about -€0.45; if all the upsides occur, EBITDA is about €36m and EPS €0.46. The forecasts sit in the middle of that range; consensus EBITDA sits in the upper third, and consensus EPS near the top.

Counter-case. The forecasts give the new team no growth credit at all (charging +3%, storage flat, no turnkey premium, no sodium-ion revenue), so they carry genuine upside. The charging sales channel is clean (Rexel reports no overstocking); the Plus platform is listed at three major distributors; Spanish and Italian registrations are up 27-78%; German storage is being built at a record rate; mobile storage tripled in H1 2026; and turnkey storage costs have fallen 78% since 2022, which lifts developers' returns. If the commercial plan works, FY28 EBITDA of €35m is reachable.

What would change my view. Any of the five judgements printing at its upper branch for two consecutive periods; a 2027 storage order book above €90m by December 2026.

Why I change no forecast input. The Financial Analyst's inputs are internally consistent, reconcile to the accounts on the one line (D&A) where the brokers' figures do not, and rest on demonstrated strengths with two small asks (charging growth of 3% and storage intake of €35m a quarter). The one judgement I could have changed, giving the new team credit for growth, I have deliberately left as an explicit upside branch rather than folding it into a base case that the record does not yet support. Two gaps in the model's mechanics, not in its inputs, are set out in the end notes.

Against the market. Consensus and I agree on revenue and on the shape of FY27. We disagree by €4m on FY27 EBITDA (because of the FY26 base) and by €0.29 on FY27 EPS (because of D&A). The bullish out-year narrative (Jefferies: a 9.6-10% margin by FY30 on 12% annual growth) is held by one house and needs strengths that are not in the record.

Score: 52, set by the Rater. Above 35% gives C. I place it at the bottom of the band because the growth is the mechanical spreading of EUR 23-24m of fixed charges over a recovering EBITDA from a trough, not a strong business. Revenue grows only about 6.5% a year, all organic and grid-led, and the EBITDA margin reaches only 6.9% by FY30 against 11-18% in FY21-23. That is better than the last four years but well below the company's past, and full-definition FCF is about nil.

7Scope for upgrades to guidance, sell-side estimates and the narrative over 6-12 months

Conclusion: the scope for upgrades over the next 6-12 months is low. The probable sequence is three downgrade steps ending in August 2027, and the first plausible upgrade is to grid revenue in late 2027. An upside branch of about one in three exists if storage intake and substation volumes both surprise in the Q3 update on 4 November 2026.

Evidence.

  • Estimates: consensus FY26 EBITDA is €22.0m (range €17.4-26.1m), against the forecasts' €18.3m and management's own steer. Consensus FY27 EPS of €0.35 is held up by two brokers' D&A assumptions and one broker's EBITDA. The FY28 EPS median is €0.38 (mean €0.50, range €0.26-0.68). For FY29, a single broker forecasts €56.1m of EBITDA and €1.04 of EPS.
  • Ratings: none of the eight brokers rates the shares a buy. Price targets range from €5.70 to €14.00, with a median of €10.50.
  • Revisions: the FactSet revision figures (FY27 EPS +13% over three months and +18% over six) are an artefact of the contributor set shrinking. The twelve-month figures (EPS -23%, EBITDA -26%) show the real trend.
  • Broker narrative: the brokers' reports cover the operating story (the H2 2026 trough, the H1 2027 comparison, the price war, market-share loss, the finance director change) but not the earnings story (D&A, the definition of free cash flow, the ceiling set by the guarantee facility, and the effect of the FY26 base on FY27).

Inference. Estimates are likely to fall in three steps over the next 6-12 months, as the timeline below shows: FY26 EBITDA toward €18-19m by February 2027, FY27 EPS toward about €0.15 at the FY26 results, and FY27 EBITDA toward €25-27m by August 2027. FY28 EPS follows D&A down toward €0.25. The single-broker FY29 "consensus" will be replaced by a broader and far lower set of estimates as coverage forms; that change will read as a cut but is an artefact of coverage.

So what. The scope for upgrades in the window Richard cares about is low. The first genuine upgrades will be to grid revenue, where the forecasts sit above consensus (FY27 €233m against €229m; FY28 €258m against €248m). They could plausibly come with the Q3 2027 update and the first FY28 guidance in February 2028, 12-15 months away. Upgrading the narrative from "transition year, problem child, lumpy storage" to "grid compounder" needs two consecutive quarters of grid growth above 15%, FY27 margin guidance of 7% or more, and storage intake back above €40-50m a quarter.

Counter-case (the 30-35% branch). The branch needs Q3 storage intake above €45m, a 2027 order book above €90m by December, substations above 950 in the quarter, charging volumes flat in Q4 with price held, and H2 2026 EBITDA above €5m. Under that branch, FY26 EBITDA holds near €21-22m, FY27 EBITDA holds, only the EPS line is cut, and the narrative turns a year early. Short covering (7.6% of the shares, about seven days of trading volume) would amplify the move, as it did in spring 2026.

What would change my view. A Q3 update that prints the upper branch on storage and substations at once; a FY27 range with a margin midpoint of 6% or more that the H1 2027 results then support.

Against the market. The Master Dashboard's sell-side momentum letter is C and its revision score is +1 (near neutral). I read both as artefacts, and I read the underlying breadth of revisions as negative through H1 2027. The ratings capitulation is complete; the capitulation in estimates is not.

Score: 15, set by the Rater. Over the next 6-12 months the likely changes are all downward. FY26 guidance is more likely met at the floor or missed (about 30% below the floor) than raised, and any FY27 range given in February is more likely to be steered down later than raised. Consensus faces three documented cut steps: FY26 EBITDA about -15% (75% likely), FY27 EPS -40 to -60% on the D&A line (70%), and FY27 EBITDA about -10% (65%). Against growth of about 5% a year these are ratios of several times minus one. The narrative has already capitulated (0% buys), which limits further damage, and an upside branch of about one in three keeps it off the floor; the fourth-set group's 18 agrees.

8Current momentum: guidance, sell-side, narrative, technicals, and peers

Conclusion: momentum is negative in guidance (none), estimates (down over twelve months, with the recent uptick an artefact), narrative (the sector is being sold as a factor) and technicals (grade D, 13% below the 200-day average). Grid peers with pricing power show strong earnings momentum, while charging and distribution-equipment peers are as weak as Alfen. Only the ratings capitulation is complete.

Evidence.

  • Guidance: no momentum. Guidance has been reiterated twice, and the last move was a cut.
  • Sell-side: twelve-month EPS revisions -23% and EBITDA revisions -26%; buy ratings 0% (down 10 points in three months); mean rating Underweight.
  • Narrative: the grid sector is being sold as a factor: grid names fell 12-20% in October while the sector leaders reported record orders. Alfen's six-month residual return against the grid basket is about -2%, so its recent fall is the sector's fall.
  • Technicals: the price of €10.38 is 13.4% below the 200-day average (€11.99) and below the 50-day (€11.39) and 150-day (€12.75) averages. The relative-strength percentile is 18. The shares are down 17.7% over three months and 16.2% over six, and up 8.2% over twelve. Technical momentum is pinned at D. The 52-week range is €8.05-19.9.
  • Peers: every stock in the 16-name sector has a technical grade of D or worse except Siemens and Landis+Gyr (C). Earnings momentum is A or B at ABB, Arteche, Cenergy, Prysmian, NKT and Legrand (record orders and raised guidance), and D or F at Pfisterer, Kempower, Landis+Gyr and R&S Group (installation bottlenecks, destocking, charging de-rating). Alfen's daily moves pair with NKT, Prysmian, ABB, Pfisterer and Fastned, and hardly at all with Arteche.
  • Read-across this month: R&S Group's capital markets day (4 November), Pfisterer's Q3 results (18 November), CATL pricing, and the Kempower and Zaptec results.

Inference. Momentum is negative or absent on every axis except one: ratings have fully capitulated. The stock has become a high-beta (1.24) way to hold the "Dutch grid" theme: it rallied 53% on that theme in spring 2026 and has given the gain back as the theme is sold. The sector's fundamental split between winners (who own a scarce slot, crew or qualification) and losers (who sell a box on a mandate) places Alfen's two moatless units with the losers and its grid unit with the winners, but the share price trades with the losers.

So what. The next six months carry a sector-factor risk that Alfen's fundamentals do not control. The Q3 update on 4 November 2026 is the first of three results that decide whether the FY27 reset happens in one step or two. The table below sets out what to read in it.

Counter-case. A heavily shorted, illiquid small cap with fully capitulated ratings is primed to move hard on any positive surprise. The price is already 48% below the June 2026 high and 22% above the 52-week low, so much of the de-rating is done.

What would change my view. Relative strength back above the 50th percentile with the 200-day average turning up; a quarter in which Alfen's residual return against the grid basket is clearly positive on its own numbers.

Against the market. The Master Dashboard grades TSR/Valuation at A on the memo's modal return. That grade rests on the P/E artefact discussed in topic 11, and Richard should read it as a question, not a rating.

Score: 27, set by the Rater. Both measures are negative, which gives D, and the parts confirm the low end of the band. Guidance has had no momentum since its last move, a cut. Twelve-month EPS is -23% and EBITDA -26%; the +13% three-month revision is a contributor-set artefact. Buy ratings have gone to 0%, and the price is below its 50-, 150- and 200-day averages and 13% under the 200-day. The comparable charging and distribution-equipment peers show the same weakness, while grid peers with pricing power are not like-for-like. The guidance has not been cut, so the parts do not take it to F.

9Riskiness and simplicity of the forecasts and expectations

Conclusion: the case is simple in thesis and complex in delivery. Its range of outcomes is wide and trackable but resolves slowly; sudden share-price risk is high because of positioning and sector beta; revenue is concentrated on one customer group and one supplier; and sector precedents favour the cautious reading. Riskiness is high; solvency risk is low.

Simplicity. The case is simple to state ("grid volume up 8-11% a year, opex held, the other two segments flat") and hard to deliver, because the lines that do not drive the thesis drive the near-term numbers. One well-evidenced driver, grid, carries more than 100% of the net EBITDA gain to FY30 and is the most predictable line. Two lumpy, price-led lines, storage and charging, make up about 55% of revenue and will produce most of the forecast error over the next 18 months. The layer of fixed charges below EBITDA turns all of that error into noise in EPS.

Fragilities, assumptions and requirements.

  • Concentration: two customers make up 34.8% of revenue under frameworks with no minimum volumes (Pfisterer's largest customer is 4.6% of its revenue); one plant; one cell supplier, with penalties on minimum volumes; one supplier of concrete housings (the Pacto chain).
  • Costs: 80% of the cost base is personnel, on 5% wage indexation.
  • Balance sheet: the guarantee facility is 65% used, which caps fixed-price storage intake; the revolving credit facility must be refinanced in 2027; intra-year net debt can reach €40-45m on swings in customer down-payments.
  • Quality of earnings: €7.5m of "one-offs" in FY26, after €5m, €25m and €2m in prior years; an interim finance director; management incentives and the bank covenant both set on the same adjusted EBITDA.

Suddenness, predictability, prevalence and materiality of share-price risks. Several risks are sudden and material, with or without fundamental justification: storage intake can swing from €54m to €11m between quarters; the trading updates are binary events; 7.6% of the shares are sold short against daily trading of USD 2.6-4.4m; the beta to a de-rating sector is 1.24; and peers create read-across every week. Other risks are trackable. Alfen's operating disclosure is unusually good (substations by country, charge points and price, backlog by delivery year, segment gross margins, the direction of personnel cost). Its earnings disclosure is poor exactly where my view diverges from consensus: it gives no segment EBITDA, no quarterly D&A or cash flow, and no split between permanent and transitional personnel. The FY26 range of outcomes closes on 17 February 2027; the FY27 range narrows only in August 2027, so nine to ten months of wide dispersion lie ahead.

Tail risks (18 months). Of the five tail risks below, only a recurrence of the substation quality problem would end the thesis. None threatens solvency.

Sector and cyclicality precedents. The precedents favour the cautious reading. Three of Richard's patterns also fit: "Turnarounds take longer than you think"; "False friends" (milestone revenue and working-capital cash masking margin); and "Cockroaches are never alone" (a finance director leaving after earlier problems).

The range of outcomes. FY26 EBITDA is €15-21m (base €18.3m, with a one-in-three chance of a margin below the 4% floor). FY27 EBITDA is €16-34m around a base of €25m. FY28 EBITDA is €21-42m. The skew is down against consensus on EBITDA, heavily down against consensus EPS, balanced around the forecasts, and slightly up on FY28 grid. The range for cash is wider than the range for earnings: FY27 free cash flow on the full definition is -€15m to +€3m.

Against the market. The sell-side's map of operating risks matches mine. It omits the ceiling set by the guarantee facility, the effect of the FY26 base on FY27, and the D&A reset; together these make the next two results riskier than the brokers' Hold ratings imply.

Score: 20, set by the Rater. The memo's FY27 EPS cone (-0.26 to +0.38 around 0.06) spans losses to profits, and the EBITDA cone (EUR 16-34m) is about a third either way, resolving only by August 2027. Risks are sudden and material: storage intake has swung from EUR 54m to 11m in a quarter, trading updates are binary, 7.6% of the capital is short and the stock has a 1.24 beta to a de-rating sector. Two customers are 34.8% of revenue on frameworks with no minimum volumes, and there is one cell supplier and one plant. The 2023-25 quality failure and the sector precedents favour caution. Net cash, low solvency risk and good operating disclosure keep it above the leveraged cases, so I sit below the groups' 28 and 38 because the cone spans the zero line.

10Where the stock is in its lifecycle

Conclusion: the stock is stalling after a false turn-up, earnings are still bottoming, and the genuine turn is dated to the H2 2027 results. This phase argues for a multiple in the lower half of the range and for entry after, not before, the FY26 results on 17 February 2027.

Evidence. The Master Dashboard's rule places the starting phase at Reinforcing, because the two-year-forward P/E of 28.2x on consensus EPS sits below the 90th-percentile guideline. The fundamentals say otherwise. Grid operations turned up two quarters ago (substations +27%), but earnings have not turned: H2 2026 is the trough half and H1 2027 will be below the prior year. Estimates are about to be cut, not raised, and buy ratings are at 0%. The stock rallied 53% to June 2026 on the grid theme and short covering, and has fallen 48% since on the H2 reality and the sector unwind. The idiosyncratic share of the stock's variance has fallen as investors first adopted it, then sold it, as a way to express the grid factor.

Inference. On Richard's six-phase scale, the share price ran a premature "turning up" in spring 2026, is now stalling, and the earnings are still bottoming. The genuine turn, when estimates and narrative move up together, is dated to the H2 2027 results: it should first show in the Q3 2027 update in November 2027 and in the FY27 results in February 2028. The FY26 results on 17 February 2027 are the event that completes the bottoming, by resetting FY27 expectations. "Reinforcing" requires delivery and upgrades, and there is neither. "Thesis broadening" happened in the market's mind in spring 2026 and has reversed.

So what. A phase between bottoming and turning up argues for the lower part of the multiple range (topic 11) and for patience on entry. For the next nine months the share price should trade on the sector factor and on the Q3 and FY26 results rather than on the recovery.

Counter-case. If the Q3 update on 4 November 2026 shows storage intake above €45m and substations above 950, the operating turn is confirmed on two of the three lines at once, and the market could skip the reset. The multiple already carries a company-specific discount, so the stalling phase has less far to fall than the price chart suggests.

What would change my view. Two consecutive results after which estimates rise; FY26 results that deliver the D&A reset without a cut to FY27 EBITDA (consensus FY27 EBITDA at the forecasts' level would mean the trough is fully priced).

Against the market. The Master Dashboard says Reinforcing; the sell-side says "transition year", which is Bottoming in Richard's terms; I say Bottoming in earnings and Stalling in price, with Turning up dated to H2 2027.

Score: 36, set by the Rater. I agree with the memo, not the computed Reinforcing. The price ran a false turn-up in spring 2026 (+53%) and has stalled since (-48%), while earnings are still bottoming (H2 2026 at a 1% margin, H1 2027 below the prior year) and estimates are about to be cut. The genuine turn is dated to the H2 2027 prints. The grid operating turn (+27% substations) and complete ratings capitulation lift it a little above a plain Stalling case, but the next six to nine months bring downgrades, not acceleration.

11The fair multiple

Conclusion: the guideline's 45x belongs to a Reinforcing phase the stock is not in, and to an earnings base too small to carry a P/E. My fair multiple is the ten-year median of about 26x two-year-forward earnings, equivalent to 9x forward EBITDA, rising to 10-11x as grid delivery is proven.

Viewforth's guideline. For the Reinforcing phase, the guideline fair multiple is 45.37x two-year-forward P/E, the 90th percentile of the stock's ten-year history. The multiple today is 28.2x on consensus EPS and 52.8x on the model's own EPS, so the guideline sits 61% above the current multiple.

My view: two corrections.

First, the phase. As topic 10 argues, the stock is between bottoming and turning up, not reinforcing. By Richard's own rule, the fair multiple for that phase sits lower in the range, where forecasts are more uncertain: between the 35th percentile (22.3x, "conservative") and the median (26.3x, "prudent"), not at the 90th.

Second, the lens. On the forecasts, two-year-forward EPS is €0.44 (FY29) at end-2027 and €0.62 at mid-2029, after €0.06-0.25 in the two years before. On earnings that small a P/E is unstable. The ten-year P/E history it is compared with was also set when charging was 40-57% of revenue, at gross margins above 40% and growing fast. The steadier lens is enterprise value to EBITDA, which both the sell-side and earlier work on Alfen use.

  • Alfen's own range: from a trough of about 7x forward EBITDA (November 2024) to an average of about 16x, which Jefferies puts about 39% above today's 9.8x.
  • Brokers: ING values Alfen at 8.5x.
  • Precedent transactions for grid assets: 11-18x (ABB's low-voltage purchase 11.1x, Vertiv 13x, Trench about 18x).
  • Grid peers: trading at the 77th-98th percentile of their own P/E histories, a premium Alfen does not deserve with 57% of its revenue moatless.

A multiple of 9-10x FY28 EBITDA is my fair range for a turning-up phase with these foundations, rising toward 11-12x only once grid volume is visibly carrying the margin (from H2 2027 onward).

The two lenses reconcile. 9x FY28 EBITDA (€30.7m), less about €25m of lease-inclusive net debt, gives €11.5 a share. €11.5 is 26x FY29 EPS of €0.44, which is the ten-year median P/E. My fair multiple is therefore about 26x two-year-forward earnings, or equivalently 9x forward EBITDA: roughly half the guideline.

Against the market. The sell-side's median target of €10.50 (Deutsche Bank on 14x P/E and 10x EV/EBIT; Jefferies on a discounted cash flow with 10% FY27 growth) is consistent with my range on the brokers' own EBITDA; on the forecasts' lower EBITDA the same multiples give €9-10. The Master Dashboard's valuation letter of B (P/E at the 34th percentile) is right in direction; its TSR/Valuation letter of A is the artefact.

Score: 38, set by the Rater. Dear on one measure and neutral on the other gives D. The neutral reading flatters, because it rests on consensus EPS the memo shows is about 85% too high; on the forecasts' EPS the P/E is 52.8x, above the 90th percentile. On EV/EBITDA the shares are about 39% below their own history, but that cheapness is largely deserved by the mix change and the stalling phase. The memo's fair value (26x, or 9x FY28 EBITDA, about EUR 11.5) sits roughly 11% above the price, so I place it in the upper middle of the band rather than at its floor.

12Total shareholder return, DuPont

Conclusion: at the model's guideline multiple, the return is +92% to end-2027 and +172% to mid-2029, almost all from "earnings" recovering from zero at a P/E that should not be applied. At my fair multiple, the return is +11% to +24% over 18 months and +55% to +70% over three years. FY30 EBITDA drives almost all of the three-year return, and grid volume drives almost all of FY30 EBITDA. The 7x trough value is €8.7, and the three-year outcome is flat if grid grows only 5% a year.

The model's return at the guideline multiple. From €10.32, the model shows +92.4% to €19.85 at the 18-month column (31 December 2027; +75% annualised) and +172.0% to €28.08 at the three-year column (30 June 2029; +46% annualised). Dividends contribute 0%. The multiple contributes -14.0%, falling from 52.8x on the model's two-year-forward EPS of about €0.20 today to 45.37x. Earnings contribute +123.8% (two-year-forward EPS rising from about €0.20 to €0.44 by end-2027) and +216.4% (to €0.62 by mid-2029).

The earnings contribution is the mechanical recovery from near zero described in topics 5 and 6. It is real as arithmetic but carries almost no information as a return, because a 2-point change in the FY27 margin assumption changes the "earnings growth" by tens of percentage points. The template's own trailing split, which attributes +947% to the multiple, makes the same point.

My return at my fair multiple: 18 months (end-2027). 26x on FY29 EPS of €0.44 gives €11.5 a share, +11% (equivalent to 9x FY28 EBITDA); at 10x FY28 EBITDA the value is €12.9, +24%. Split on the model's basis, earnings contribute +124%, the multiple -50% (from 52.8x to 26.3x) and dividends nil. The return is small because today's multiple is high only because today's EPS is depressed. On the cleaner EBITDA lens, the shares trade today at 9.8x FY27 EBITDA and would trade at 9-10x FY28 EBITDA at end-2027, so the return is roughly FY27-to-FY28 EBITDA growth (+23%) less the drift in net debt (about -6%), plus or minus a point of re-rating. The downside is €8.7 at the 7x trough multiple (-16%), and about €6.5 (-37%) at 7x if FY27 EBITDA is cut to €22m.

My return at my fair multiple: three years (mid-2029). 9-10x FY30 EBITDA of €41.3m, less about €20m of net debt, gives €16-18 a share, +55% to +70% (15-19% annualised). Almost all of it comes from EBITDA growth (from €25m to €41m), with no re-rating. If grid grows 5% a year, FY30 EBITDA is about €30m and the shares are worth about €11.5, a flat outcome. At a precedent-transaction multiple of 13x in a friendly deal, the shares are worth €24-25.

What drives the return. In order of importance: grid volume; the recovery of the multiple from 9x toward 11-12x as grid delivery is proven; storage intake; and the FY27 EPS reset, which has no direct effect on an EBITDA valuation but is the event that sets the entry price. Dividends and buybacks add nothing: full-definition free cash flow is about nil to FY30, and a 10% buyback would need debt at 8.5% interest and would add only €0.01-0.02 of EPS.

Against the market. The sell-side median target of €10.50 implies about 1% upside. The market and I agree on the 12-18-month return. We disagree on when the three-year return becomes visible (late 2027) and on what it depends on (grid volume alone).

Score: 41, set by the Rater. About +7% sits in D, which maps to about 42. I place it at 41, a point lower, because two forces offset each other: the lower tail is fat and comes first (three downgrade steps before any upgrade), while the three-year check is supportive (+55% to +70% if grid volume delivers, flat if it grows only 5% a year). Nothing comes from dividends or buybacks.

13Summary conclusion

Alfen is a national grid franchise with two commodity hardware units attached, run by a credible repairer who has fixed the balance sheet and the cost base but has not yet shown a margin.

The case is a volume case in one segment. Over the next 12-24 months the investment case rests on Dutch substations growing 8-11% a year on record operator budgets and a permitting path dated in law, rationed by the operators' own technicians and permits, at a gross margin the buyers cap at 22-25%. That volume carries the whole net EBITDA gain of the forecast horizon and nearly all of the three-year return; nothing else in the company adds value net of cost inflation.

The expectations gap closes through disappointment before it closes through discovery. The earnings trough is still ahead (H2 2026 at a 1% margin; H1 2027 below the prior year). Consensus FY27 EPS is about 85% too high because of a D&A line the accounts contradict, and the upper half of the sell-side has not absorbed management's H2 steer. Expect six to nine months of downgrades first.

The valuation is fair for a case that has not yet turned. The P/E lens and the Reinforcing-phase guideline produce a +92% return that is an artefact of near-zero earnings. On EBITDA, the shares trade at a company-specific discount that is fair for a stalling case that has not yet turned: +11-24% to end-2027, +55-70% over three years if grid delivers, flat if it does not, with a trough value of €8-9.

Why the case is worth watching rather than dismissing.

  • The one driver that matters, grid volume, is the best-evidenced line in the file, and Alfen reports it every quarter.
  • The multiple is driven by company factors and is already discounted.
  • The ratings base has capitulated, and 7.6% of the shares are sold short.
  • The asymmetry turns from negative to positive at a dated event, the FY26 results on 17 February 2027, which the market can see coming.

The practical posture: let the FY26 results reset set the price, then buy the grid-volume upgrade. The Q3 update on 4 November 2026 is the first of three tests: storage intake above €40m, substations above 950, and an implied charging price at or above €950.

End notes

Definitions. All money is in EUR millions unless stated. EBITDA is the company's adjusted basis, which is also the brokers' basis. "The forecasts" are the Financial Analyst's model (update 1). "Consensus" is the FactSet median at 28 October 2026. Segment names: grid is Smart Grid Solutions (SGS), storage is Energy Storage Systems (ESS), and charging is EV Charging (EVC). The structuurregime is the Dutch statutory regime for large companies, under which the supervisory board appoints the management board.

Forecast inputs. This memo changes none of the Financial Analyst's forecast inputs; topic 6 gives the reasons.

Model notes for the Financial Analyst. A review flagged two gaps in the model's mechanics, not in its inputs. First, the model holds H1 2026 on the reported basis (EBITDA €11.0m) rather than the adjusted basis (€16.4m); this inflates the model's H2 2026 margin to about 3.7% against the intended 1.0%, and gives FY26 EPS of -€0.13 against a like-for-like -€0.17. Second, the model's working-capital line cannot carry the unwinding of storage down-payments. Both are fixes, not changes of view. The Financial Analyst should hold the H1 2026 actual on the adjusted basis so that the 1.0% H2 2026 margin is used as written, start FY26 year-end net cash from the June 2026 balance, and state the total return on an EV/EBITDA basis beside the P/E basis while forecast EPS is below about €0.30.

Visual sources. Default charts and tables come from the Financial Analyst's model (update 1), FactSet and the Master Dashboard, as noted under each. Charts drawn for this page take their figures from the memo; where a figure is derived rather than stated (the half-year revenue and EBITDA path, the storage-and-charging step in the FY26-FY30 bridge, the segment gross-profit shares, the EPS implied at the FY27 EBITDA boundaries, the 13x three-year return, and the fixed-charge line set against EBITDA), the note under the chart says so.

Colours. Blue for history and upside, violet for consensus, orange for the forecasts (Viewforth), aqua for peers and precedents, red for falls and risks. Grades: A 90 to 100, B 75 to 89, C 50 to 74, D 25 to 49, F 1 to 24.

Our model keeps one reporting basis for history and forecasts. The checks below suggest that consensus may use a different basis for some lines, so part of the gap between our forecasts and consensus on those lines may not be a difference of view. Nothing has been adjusted in the model.

What the checks found:

  • FY2025 earnings per share: -0.01 on the brokers' basis against 0.17 on our model's basis (-106.0%).
  • Consensus EBIT for FY2026 is -0.76, -111.7% against 6.46 in FY2025 on our model's basis; consensus revenue moves +4.3%.
  • Consensus net income for FY2026 is -2.41, -167.1% against 3.59 in FY2025 on our model's basis; consensus revenue moves +4.3%.
  • Consensus earnings per share for FY2026 is -0.13, -179.0% against 0.17 in FY2025 on our model's basis; consensus revenue moves +4.3%.

Facts in the data file that commonly explain such a gap:

  • Amortisation of acquired intangibles over the last twelve months: -6.2 before tax (-0.28 per share); our model's FY2025 history does not exclude it (its EBITA equals EBIT). Brokers' adjusted figures often exclude it.
  • Hybrid bond coupons and capitalised leases are not in the data file; check the company's reporting where relevant.

How to read this page

Every rating of this stock on one page: the Rater's 1-100 number, its letter and the Rater's own reason (at most three sentences, taken from the ratings file; nothing newly written). The number is the company's approximate standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10; 50 = typical). A letter follows its item's rule: rank among the stocks scored (A the top 10%; B+ and B the next 15%; C+, C and C- the next 25%; D the next 25%; F the bottom 25%); or Richard's cut-offs on the measure for the four numerical topics (forecast financials, current momentum, the fair multiple, total shareholder return). On the change-forces items the number carries a sign (50 = neither positive nor negative) and the letter is the rank, so read the two together. "9th of 30 stocks scored" is the stock's place on that item. A dashed badge is provisional (fewer than 30 stocks scored).
